answer.rationale: memory_c2 is the only record showing a vendor already proven to deliver lower unit cost with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—critical because the incumbent has refused to reopen price and finance demands an 18% cut. memory_c6 confirms multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing, so if I switch to the low-cost vendor I can structure the new contract as multi-year to capture additional unit-cost reduction. The 14-day expiry and no auto-renew clause make delay dangerous; the assembly line at 94% with no buffer means I cannot absorb even a short delivery gap, but memory_c2's record of quick onboarding and accurate invoicing directly addresses that risk. Deferring (memory_c5) preserves budget flexibility but does not meet the 18% cut mandate. Adding a second source (memory_c3) reduces single-point-of-failure risk but does not reduce spend and I only have one decision slot. Negotiating with the incumbent (memory_c4) is blocked because they have already refused to reopen price this cycle. Therefore switching primary supply to the proven low-cost vendor, structured as a multi-year commitment, is the single action that best minimizes total cost of ownership without increasing delivery risk.
